title: Heat-up of reheat furnace 4 after refractory repair
summary: Prove the furnace safe to fire after a lining repair, light off, hold the mandatory cure schedule, and hand the unit to the mill at 1150 C.

warnings.label: Step 6 records a pass or fail but the procedure never says what a failed proven test is worth, so the crew can sign a line it did not pump up
The purge is written as a duration, not as a demonstrated condition, so nothing in the procedure proves the chamber is free of gas before the pilot is lit
Step 11 says to confirm the rate on the controller face but the two furnaces share a panel and the faceplates were swapped during the retrofit
Step 12 puts the cure schedule in direct conflict with a mill that is waiting for slabs, and the procedure does not say who wins
The shell survey is the only barrier against a hot spot, and it is performed by the same person running the whole heat-up

steps.title: Confirm the completion certificate and that the permit is closed
steps.text: Confirm the refractory contractor's completion certificate for the repaired area, and that the work permit is closed and the scaffolding is out.

errors.text: The certificate is in the office upstairs and the permit was closed by phone. Nobody looked at the scaffold
Signed off the certificate for furnace 5, whose repair finished in the same week on the same paperwork stack
Permit closed by the authority, but the scaffold was still standing when he looked

steps.title: Walk the peeking ports and confirm nothing is left inside
steps.text: Confirm no tools, timber or shuttering left inside the chamber. Walk the peeking ports with a torch.

errors.text: Looked in one port from the platform. The far end of the chamber is not visible from any port
Torch battery was flat, so he did the quick version
Satisfied because the contractor said they had cleaned up

steps.title: Open the flue damper to the purge position
steps.text: Open the flue damper to the purge position.

errors.text: Moved the recirculation damper, which is on the same shaft and has the same handle
Assumed the night shift left it open because the furnace was already cold
The mechanism is stiff and it came up three quarters of the way. The handle looks open

steps.title: Start the combustion air fan and purge for not less than fifteen minutes
steps.text: Start the combustion air fan and purge the chamber for not less than fifteen minutes with the damper open to atmosphere.

errors.text: Ran the fan, went to check the gas train, came back at seven minutes and called the purge done
Started the fan from the panel and left for the pilot. Nobody confirmed the air was actually moving at the damper
The mill had two heats waiting, so he took five minutes as good enough for a cold chamber
Purged with the damper still in the run position instead of the purge position

steps.title: Prove the main burner gas valve tight
steps.text: Carry out the gas valve proven test on the main burner train per MSR-11 section 4: isolate, pressurise to 100 mbar, observe the decay for two minutes. Record the result on the heat-up sheet.

errors.text: The train was already pressurised from the night shift, so he signed the line without pumping it up or timing the decay
The test gauge needle was stuck at zero. A decay from 100 to 40 mbar looked like no movement at all
Proved the block valve, which is the one the interlock watches, and not the burner valve that faces the furnace
Ran the test on the furnace 5 train, whose panel tag was moved in the retrofit

steps.title: Confirm the flame supervision scanner on burner 1 is clear and proven
steps.text: Confirm the flame supervision UV scanner on burner 1 is clear and proven.

errors.text: The scanner has been noisy for months and the panel lamp is dim, so it reads the same as always
Wiped the sight glass, did not run the prove test because it trips the burner lockout timer
Covered the sight glass to stop it alarming and forgot to uncover it

steps.title: Check the shell survey points are reachable and the pyrometer is ready
steps.text: Confirm the shell temperature survey points on the repaired roof are reachable and that the pyrometer battery is good.

errors.text: The scaffold to the roof is signed out to another trade, so the survey will not happen tonight
Battery checked, emissivity tape not, so the readings will be meaningless

steps.title: Light the pilot on burner 1 and confirm flame on the scanner
steps.text: Light the pilot on burner 1 and confirm the flame on the scanner.

errors.text: Pilot did not light, he did not wait for the scanner, and he went on to the main gas anyway
Cracked the main gas at the same time as the pilot to save a trip back to the panel
Took the standing scanner lamp for a flame indication

steps.title: Admit main gas at the minimum firing position
steps.text: Admit main gas at the minimum firing position.

errors.text: The burner lit on the pilot alone and he never opened the main, then set a ramp that the pilot cannot hold
Opened the bypass train, which has no flame supervision behind it
Admitted gas before the fan interlock had settled, and the train tripped the burner management shut with the valve already open

steps.title: If the burner does not light, lock off and re-purge for fifteen minutes
steps.text: If the burner does not light on the first attempt, lock off, re-purge for fifteen minutes.

errors.text: A second purge is forty minutes he does not have, so he tried the pilot again instead
Went to find the shop engineer first, and the gas kept coming while he was on the radio

steps.title: Set the ramp rate to 60 C/h and confirm the controller shows it
steps.text: Set the ramp rate to 60 C/h on controller TRC-4C and confirm the rate shown on the controller face matches the rate you entered.

errors.text: Entered 60 in the field the manual page calls degrees per minute. The controller accepted 3600 C/h and the furnace took it
Set it on TRC-5C. The faceplates came back from the retrofit the wrong way round and nobody has reported it
Confirmed the number on the face but the profile was already running from the previous heat
Typed 60, hit enter, and the controller was still in cascade manual so it ignored him

steps.title: Hold 60 C/h until the lining moisture is below one per cent
steps.text: Hold the ramp at 60 C/h until the zone reaches 300 C. Watch the lining moisture readout; above 1% the rate is not to be increased whatever the mill asks for.

errors.text: The mill wanted three slabs by the end of the shift, so he moved the rate to 300 C/h with the moisture still at two per cent
Left the cure to the controller profile and walked away
Read the moisture from the previous entry on the sheet because the readout was stuck

steps.title: Survey the shell at the four points and stop the ramp above 260 C
steps.text: Record the shell temperature at the four survey points every thirty minutes. A reading over 260 C is a hot spot: stop the ramp and call the shop engineer. Do not cover a hot spot by increasing the air.

errors.text: Took the readings through the insulation blanket on the roof, so the repair patch itself was never surveyed
Pyrometer emissivity was still set for the old painted shell, and the true temperature was 60 C above what he wrote down
Found a hot spot and opened the cooling air over it instead of stopping the ramp, exactly as the procedure forbids

steps.title: Notify the mill and record the heat-up sheet
steps.text: Notify the mill that furnace 4 is at temperature and record the finish time, the cure curve and your initials on the heat-up sheet.

errors.text: Sheet filled in the next day from memory, so a skipped cure stage never appears on the record
Recorded the controller setpoint as the zone temperature, hiding a twenty degree lag behind the thermocouple
Told the mill it was at temperature to get the slabs moving, at 1050 C

steps.title: Emergency: stop firing on a bang or a lifted roof
steps.text: If you hear a bang or see the roof lift, stop firing at the local emergency stop, close the main gas valve, and evacuate the front of the furnace. Do not open a peeking port.

errors.text: The bang was attributed to the refractory ticking over as it dries, which is a thing crews say
